newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds end softer on fresh supply.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds end softer on fresh supply.

text.p: FUTURES CASH YIELD
*Australian bonds soften through the afternoon session following the A$600 million bond tender to levels they were at before Friday's release of U.S. payrolls.
*TCV to tender A$200 million of new 2008 stock on Wednesday.
Australian bonds maintained their softer opening tone through the afternoon, falling to levels they were at before the release of U.S. payrolls last Friday.
The A$600 million government bond tender added to the softer tone of the market, traders said, and although the market could weaken further, the underlying sentiment was still positive.

"Probably a little more stock went to the street than people were expecting -- they probably hadn't done that much protection before the tender," one trader said, adding this was because the market was wary of the tender being taken out by one player, as happened at the last government bond tender.
"So they were probably a little reluctant to go in short, so we've seen a bit of hedging since, but I think that's pretty much been digested now," he said.
The tender saw the A$200 million January 2001 bonds go at a weighted average of 7.098 percent, and the A$400 million of benchmark November 2006 bonds went at 7.603 percent.
Bonds had already been softer through the morning after the U.S. market partially corrected its strong rally following the weaker than expected payrolls data on Friday.

The Treasury Corporation of Victoria (TCV) announced a A$200 million tender for Wednesday. A new 7.50 percent August 2008 bond will be issued, following completion of the consolidation of the 12.50 percent July 2000 line into other TCV stocks.
The key local event for the market is Thursday's employment data for September.
Economists surveyed by Reuters expect employment to fall by 7,500, and for the unemployment rate to come in at 8.6 percent.
Such an outcome would be supportive of the market view that a November rate cut is likely, traders said.
Spreads to U.S. continue to widen after closing last week at 71 and 100 basis points, with traders seeing potential for U.S. to further outperform in the near term.

Corrective tone to market sees bonds pull back from overbought territory on relative strength indices. Initial resistance now seen as last week's highs of 92.395 on the 10-year contract and 93.07 on the three years.
